steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: So you're finally here.
Hui-chieh.
Hui-chieh:
The storm hasn't broken for days. The whole valley's snowed over.
The raspberry bushes still haven't budded. It's like spring'll never come.
We're trapped here, starving, dressed thin, and every silent day we pass waiting for the snow to melt drives us out of our minds.
You know, there's something about it all I find odd.
We've never once had a smooth time of it. Any better circumstances, and they'd go to shit fast the moment I get involved.
Maybe it really is like the Lungmenites say. I'm a bad omen. Nothing good comes of being around me.
Reminds me of something from a hell of a long time ago.
I've been thinking how I need to share my thoughts with you, in order to find peace.
December 14th
Third year without the Black Snake
A small Ursus hamlet

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Talulah, get back here! You can't let them see you like that, for heaven's sakes.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Don't worry! I'm coming in now.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Why won't you just take those clothes off?! I've said it over and over, they'll bring those damned bugs around!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Those big, black, poisonous bugs... One bite and a whole field goes barren!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I always wear my normal clothes, don't I? I've only been wearing these lately because I had to be outside.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You remember the gentleman who gave me these clothes, don't you? The handsome one. He wouldn't recognize me in anything else.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I believe destiny will send him to me again. When that time comes, you and your husband can both live happily ever after.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Bah! Talulah... Talulah! A bald-faced liar, that's what you are. What about everything you said before, then?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Oh. What was it I said before? I've forgotten. It was the same, wasn't it?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: You said your father gave you these clothes as a birthday gift!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: You said he was robbed blind by some ring-headed foreigner, and you ran off crying, these clothes soaked in his blood!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: You're all over the place... The time before that was a different story too!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Ah, so I can't keep it straight? Your memory's just wonderful.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Don't suck up to me! Always talking complete nonsense... I've got a foot in the grave, but look at you, running an old coot like me in circles. Don't you feel even a bit of shame?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Ah. I'm sorry, that's wrong of me. Really.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Now sit down! Don't bother with your clothes! Driving me up the wall!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Chop, chop! Polish off that lunch already. You told me you'd be back by noon and the sun's almost down!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I left the soup on for you, but it's nearly boiled dry now. You may as well be having your supper at this rate!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Oh, dear Majesty, how could our little girl turn out this way...?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Get that down, you. The old man still wants you for something. Oh, that miserable drunk! Where's he run off now...? You'll have to find him yourself.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Alright, I get it.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Hmph! You grew up so well, but not a single true word comes out of your mouth! Just like all those sweet-talking youngsters in the city!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I nearly got swindled once when I was younger... There's nothing good about them!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Enough... I've heard this one a hundred times.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Talking back! Right... here. Oh, come on, take your plate now! And eat your bread, snappity-snap!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Don't rush like that! You'll choke!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: ...*Sigh*, you were all soaked in blood the day you showed up, though.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I still get chills thinking about it, Talulah. If you weren't one of those good kids, the old man would've split your head open with a hatchet right then and there.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Who can even tell if someone else is good or bad at a single glance...?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: That day you ran here, it was an evening dark as dark was, with all beasts crawling outside. Burdenbeasts or meatbeasts, they never stopped howling! Really made me uneasy...

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: And then, and then that thing you were carrying...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Unf, pff... *cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: What a big knife it was! I'd never seen one so big in all my years!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: That was a sword... a sword! Not a knife. And don't take it to clear out mountain paths again. That's not what it's for.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: And by the way! Didn't we agree never to speak of that again? I'm getting upset.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Whoops, my big mouth! Pfeh! Oh, Emperor above! I won't say a word more, not a single word of it again! Oh, Your Majesty, forgive an old blabbermouth for her careless slip!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: That's enough. Surely the Emperor's in no place to care. He's living it up just fine in his grand old city, and us? We can't even find potatoes to eat next week. He couldn't do anything for us, even if he wanted to.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: For that matter, I'm wondering if you even know who the Emperor is now?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: How rude!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The soup... are we out of salt?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Yes! We ran out a while ago. The salt jar went empty last night! Hmph, you're just as wasteful as that old man! Eating all our salt... you'll pickle yourselves dead!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: And Lord knows what in the world you're up to when you leave for days at a time! You come back with nothing, no money, not even a thing to eat! A girl driving this house to ruin...!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I get it, I get it. I'm changing it out now.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: So healthy you are! You ought to be working!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Don't bother. I had a chat with Alina just a minute ago. She'll bring us some salt. Now look at you!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Alina is a lot more reliable than you! She likes her studying, she gets hands-on with her work, and you still can't even sew your own clothes!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...To each their own.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Eh? What do you mean?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Everyone has her own ambitions.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: So what ambitions have you got? Ought to find someone good, a strong lad 'n' lass! If we leave you to do the work, mossoat'll be rotting underground before long.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I haven't slacked once on the yearly farmwork.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: You've only been here how many years?!
Talulah never falls behind on her work. Please stop scolding her.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Alina! You need to help me talk some sense into her, or else she'll keep going on like this, and...

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And there's not much wrong with that.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Oh, at last, you're here. You're the only one who knows how to quiet her down.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: So you're all grown up, are you! Think you're a noble just because you draped yourself in some uniform you got from Lord-knows-where? Small as you are, you put on airs anyway! Where'd you learn that...?!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I have work to do! You two eat up. If you're hungry, Alina. Talulah, don't eat too much! Leave some for Alina.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Alright, alright... alright.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: I'll be fine, Ma'am. Thank you.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah, I've brought some salt over. The salt merchant will be here next week, so remember to buy some then.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Thank you so, so much, Alina. Without you, she'd be going on for another twenty minutes.

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: I can hear you!

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Where'd you go this time?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Nowhere, just out for a walk to feel the wind. Right, the landscape painting you wanted.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Ah, you actually remembered. Thank you, thank you a lot, Talulah.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: This brush type... This isn't by the local painters.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: The old painter in Shmyr only knows hard strokes. I can't imagine him using a feather brush. These soft tips, this was a nighteye's plumage... from before it molted.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah, you went to the city.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...Can't hide anything from you.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Why hide things from me? I'm not Gendarmerie. Or a tax collector.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You don't need to know about any of it. It's danger all around there.

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: And you're in the thick of it, then?

The deer facing her seemed almost supernatural. The white-haired Draco felt, deep down, that if you didn't want Alina to know what was happening, your best option was not to let those things happen at all.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm just saying... Alina, you don't need to worry about th—

steps.name: Ursus Farmer
steps.text: Trouble! There's trouble...!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: What's all the racket about?! Storming in without even knocking! I don't know what I'll do if the bolt's broken!

steps.name: Ursus Farmer
steps.text: The... The Infected Patrol Unit!

steps.name: Ursus Farmer
steps.text: Your old man brought this rabble on us!

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Alina
steps.text: Talulah! Where are you going?

steps.name: Old Woman
steps.text: Oh, the knife! Alina, don't let her wave that thing around!

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: Let me repeat myself, old boy. I could just break your leg and come in all the same.

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: You've already come searching before! What're you here for now?! We can't even afford your taxes anymore! What more do you want to wring out of us?!

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: This is a routine inspection! We don't care how you try to sweeten the pot this time, we're mandated to inspect every two years... If we don't carry this out, then we're all in for the whip.

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: But if you just consent...

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: We can't give anything anymore! We've got nothing to give! No money, no jewelry, not even any more food!

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: The hell are you going on for?

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: This is a routine inspection! Out of the way!

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: Sir, sir! Officer, sir, we've got nothing left to give, honest to heaven! If you need to take something with you, just take me, for God's sakes!

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: I said OUT OF THE WAY!

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: Agh!

steps.name: Old Man
steps.text: Guh... My leg...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: Hm? Some girl from somewhere...

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: —Hey. Your clothes there. Where'd you come from? No farmer could afford to wear those.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm asking. What are you doing?

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: Not a step closer! What do you think you're doing? Have you seen your eyes...? Hah, don't you look terrifying!

steps.name: Infected Patrol Unit
steps.text: —Do I see a death wish?!
